fieldFixes.summary: Customer Commons was spun out of ProjectVRM as a nonprofit that takes no contributions from commercial entities; it is now a 501(c)(3) (the IRS exemption on record was issued in November 2018). The date is reported inconsistently: in January 2012 ProjectVRM called it 'just in the planning stages', aiming to have it running when The Intention Economy came out that May, and Customer Commons' own website says it was established in 2012, while the MyTerms FAQ dates the spin-off to 2013. MyTerms says it was created to host a roster of standard personal privacy terms, on the model Creative Commons set for copyright licences. Four of its board members — Mary Hodder, Iain Henderson, Joyce Searls and Doc Searls — were involved in IEEE 7012 from the start.
fieldFixes.locationNote: Customer Commons' own office is not given in the sources; mapped to its Berkman/ProjectVRM origin (approximate; its IRS address today is San Rafael, California). Founding date: customercommons.org was live by November 2011 (Internet Archive), ProjectVRM described it as in planning in January 2012, the site's footer says 'Established in 2012', and the MyTerms FAQ says 2013 — shown as 2012–2013.
